objective: Register a separate, finite future implementation of APBRA self-service company creation, initial owner bootstrap, membership and bounded user-profile lifecycle integrated with the merged APBRA-172 session foundation; this governance PR changes no application behavior.
requirements: Jira APBRA-151 Story 10251 under APBRA-160; Haseeb's 2026-10-02 owner decision, Jira comment 10376 and 2026-10-03 APBRA-151 mission. APBRA-151 was To Do at the live 2026-10-03 source refresh; APBRA-160 was In Progress, APBRA-172 Done and APBRA-173 To Do.

Consume an APBRA-172 validated, active application identity and session. Resolve existing active membership and eligible invitation before the ordinary no-membership Create Company / Workspace handoff; never reimplement OIDC or use external claims, email, domain, UPN or IdP group as company authority.

A server-authoritative PostgreSQL transaction creates an immutable internal APBRA company ID and exactly its creator's initial COMPANY_OWNER membership with safe audit provenance. Browser input cannot select creator identity, role, provider subject or another company's authority.

Company creation must be replay-safe and concurrency-safe: the same actor, idempotency key and materially identical command yield the same committed result; a reused key with a different command fails; concurrent requests cannot produce duplicate or ownerless companies.

Provide bounded company name or handle validation and disambiguation without treating a familiar organisation name as legal ownership. Do not invent globally exclusive commercial names, reserved customer names, numerical rate ceilings, public terms or pricing absent accepted policy.

Support the accepted company membership and bounded user-profile lifecycle with server-authoritative owner permissions, invitation integration, role/deactivation checks and last-owner protection. Preserve exact private-case grants, multi-company selection and tenant isolation after company creation.

Keep local/test bootstrap from binding a synthetic identity to a user-created company merely because its display name matches a fixture. The bootstrap correction is limited to the two exact bootstrap paths in the future allowlist; it is not live account migration or runtime tenant auto-join.
adrs: Reuse the existing APBRA company/tenant, identity, session, invitation and audit structures where safe; do not create a duplicate organisation security aggregate or a second authentication stack.

Authentication, company membership, exact private-resource grants, subscription entitlement, Power BI/Fabric consent and Azure management authority remain independent; COMPANY_OWNER is company-scoped and never platform, Power BI or Azure administration.

Company display name and optional slug are presentation and namespace values, not security identity or proof of legal ownership. APBRA company ID remains an immutable internal identifier independent of external tenant, email domain or cloud subscription.
Idempotency and uniqueness require database-backed transaction and constraints, not a Python-only check; audit creation once, preserve immutable provenance and reject cross-actor replay.
Profile email and display fields are mutable attributes, not identity-linking keys; no silent cross-provider account link. Preserve APBRA-175 deployment portability and NO HARDCODING.

Registration-only branch changes governance files. Future runtime implementation authority becomes effective only after hosted CI, genuinely separate exact-head review and Haseeb's manual merge of the registration PR.
